title: Conspiracy Against Nehemiah

questions.question: Who sent a message to Nehemiah to meet at Ono?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:2 (ESV): "Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, 'Come and let us meet together at Hakkephirim in the plain of Ono.'"

questions.question: How many times did they send the same message to Nehemiah?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:4 (ESV): "And they sent to me four times in this way..."

questions.question: What was Nehemiah’s response to their invitation?
options: I am doing a great work and I cannot come down
questions.correctAnswer: I am doing a great work and I cannot come down
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:3 (ESV): "...I am doing a great work and I cannot come down..."

questions.question: Who was hired to frighten Nehemiah into sinning?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:10-13 (ESV): "...he was hired... that I should be afraid and act in this way and sin..."

questions.question: How many days did it take to finish the wall?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:15 (ESV): "So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-two days."

questions.question: What was the content of the open letter sent the fifth time?
options: Ideally, you and the Jews intend to rebel; that is why you are building the wall
questions.correctAnswer: Ideally, you and the Jews intend to rebel; that is why you are building the wall
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:6 (ESV): "...It is reported among the nations... that you and the Jews intend to rebel..."

questions.question: Where is the plain of Ono located?
options: It is not specified, but near Lod
questions.correctAnswer: It is not specified, but near Lod

questions.question: Who was the prophetess mentioned as trying to frighten Nehemiah?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:14 (ESV): "...and the prophetess Noadiah and the rest of the prophets who wanted to make me afraid."

questions.question: Why specifically did the wall's completion dishearten the enemies?
options: They perceived that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God
questions.correctAnswer: They perceived that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:16 (ESV): "...for they perceived that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God."

questions.question: To whom was Tobiah related by marriage?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:18 (ESV): "For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah..."

questions.question: What did Shemaiah propose Nehemiah do?
options: Let us meet together in the house of God, within the temple. Let us close the doors... for they are coming to kill you
questions.correctAnswer: Let us meet together in the house of God, within the temple. Let us close the doors... for they are coming to kill you
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:10 (ESV): "...Let us meet together in the house of God... for they are coming to kill you..."

questions.question: Why did Nehemiah refuse to enter the temple?
options: Should such a man as I run away? And what man such as I could go into the temple and live?
questions.correctAnswer: Should such a man as I run away? And what man such as I could go into the temple and live?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:11 (ESV): "But I said, 'Should such a man as I run away? And what man such as I could go into the temple and live?'"

questions.question: Who was Tobiah's son?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:18 (ESV): "...and his son Jehohanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam..."

questions.question: What month was the wall finished?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:15 (ESV): "...on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul..."

questions.question: What were the nobles of Judah doing during this time?
options: Sending letters to Tobiah and receiving letters from him
questions.correctAnswer: Sending letters to Tobiah and receiving letters from him
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:17 (ESV): "Moreover, in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah..."

key_verse_text: And I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work and I cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?”
